name: Chapter 6: Equilibrium
description: Physical and chemical equilibria, Kc and Kp, Q, ΔG and K, Le Chatelier, acids and bases, pH, Ka and Kb, hydrolysis, buffers and Ksp

cards.term: What is equilibrium?
cards.definition: The state where the rates of the forward and reverse processes are equal, so composition stays constant

cards.term: Three classes of reactions by extent at equilibrium?
cards.definition: Nearly complete; only small product formed; comparable amounts of reactants and products

cards.term: What is ionic equilibrium?
cards.definition: Equilibrium involving ions in aqueous solution

cards.term: Ice and water in a thermos at 273 K: why is it "dynamic"?
cards.definition: Molecules keep moving between ice and water at equal rates; masses stay constant

cards.term: Define normal melting (freezing) point.
cards.definition: Temperature at which solid and liquid are in equilibrium at 1 atm

cards.term: What is equilibrium vapour pressure?
cards.definition: Constant pressure of vapour when rate of evaporation = rate of condensation at a given T

cards.term: Drying agents used in the vapour-pressure box?
cards.definition: Anhydrous CaCl₂ or P₄O₁₀

cards.term: Higher vapour pressure means?
cards.definition: More volatile, lower boiling point

cards.term: Why can’t an open watch glass of water reach equilibrium?
cards.definition: It is an open system: vapour disperses, so condensation stays below evaporation

cards.term: Define normal boiling point. Water’s?
cards.definition: T at which liquid and vapour are in equilibrium at 1.013 bar; water 100 °C

cards.term: Why does water boil below 100 °C in the hills?
cards.definition: Lower atmospheric pressure at high altitude

cards.term: Examples of solid ⇌ vapour equilibrium?
cards.definition: Iodine (violet vapour), camphor, NH₄Cl

cards.term: How was dynamic equilibrium in saturated sugar solution proved?
cards.definition: Adding radioactive sugar: radioactivity later appears in both solid and solution

cards.term: Henry’s law?
cards.definition: Mass of gas dissolved in a given mass of solvent is ∝ the pressure of the gas above it; decreases as T rises

cards.term: Why does soda water fizz on opening and later go flat?
cards.definition: CO₂ was dissolved under high pressure; at lower pressure solubility falls until it matches atmospheric pCO₂

cards.term: Features of physical equilibria
cards.definition: H₂O(l) ⇌ H₂O(g): p(H₂O) at given T; H₂O(s) ⇌ H₂O(l): Melting point at fixed p; Sugar(s) ⇌ Sugar(soln): Solute concentration at given T; CO₂(g) ⇌ CO₂(aq): [CO₂(aq)]/[CO₂(g)] at given T

cards.text: Physical equilibria: possible only in a {{c1::closed system}}; both processes occur at the {{c2::same rate}}; all measurable properties stay {{c3::constant}}.

cards.term: Why does the forward rate fall and reverse rate rise as a reaction proceeds?
cards.definition: Reactants deplete and products accumulate until the rates are equal

cards.term: Can equilibrium be approached from either side?
cards.definition: Yes

cards.term: How did deuterium prove ammonia equilibrium is dynamic?
cards.definition: Mixing H₂/NH₃ and D₂/ND₃ equilibria gave NH₂D, NHD₂, HD: reactions never stop

cards.term: Classroom model of dynamic equilibrium (box)?
cards.definition: Transferring coloured water between two cylinders with glass tubes until levels stop changing

cards.term: Who proposed the law of mass action, and when?
cards.definition: Guldberg and Waage (Norway), 1864

cards.term: Why "mass action"?
cards.definition: Concentration was once called "active mass"

cards.term: Kc for aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD?

cards.term: Kc for N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃: [N₂] 1.5×10⁻², [H₂] 3.0×10⁻², [NH₃] 1.2×10⁻² M? (Problem 6.1)
cards.definition: 3.55 × 10²

cards.term: Kc for N₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2NO: [N₂] 3.0×10⁻³, [O₂] 4.2×10⁻³, [NO] 2.8×10⁻³? (Problem 6.2)
cards.definition: 0.622

cards.term: Homogeneous equilibrium: define and examples.
cards.definition: All species in one phase: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃; Fe³⁺ + SCN⁻ ⇌ Fe(SCN)²⁺

cards.term: Relation between Kp and Kc?
cards.definition: \( K_p = K_c (RT)^{\Delta n} \), Δn = gaseous moles of products − reactants

cards.term: Value of R to use with Kp in bar?
cards.definition: 0.0831 bar L mol⁻¹ K⁻¹

cards.term: When is Kp = Kc?
cards.definition: When Δn = 0, e.g. H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI

cards.term: Kc for PCl₃ + Cl₂ ⇌ PCl₅: [PCl₃] = [Cl₂] = 1.59, [PCl₅] = 1.41 M? (Problem 6.3)
cards.definition: 1.41 / 1.59² = 0.558

cards.term: Equilibrium concentrations from Kc
cards.definition: 0.067 M products, 0.033 M reactants

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Problem 6.4

CO + H₂O ⇌ CO₂ + H₂, Kc = 4.24 at 800 K; start 0.10 M each of CO and H₂O.

Let x = [CO₂] = [H₂].
  1. x²/(0.1 − x)² = 4.24
  2. Take root: x/(0.1 − x) = 2.06
  3. ?
  4. [CO] = [H₂O] = 0.033 M; [CO₂] = [H₂] = 0.067 M
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Problem 6.4

CO + H₂O ⇌ CO₂ + H₂, Kc = 4.24 at 800 K; start 0.10 M each of CO and H₂O.

Let x = [CO₂] = [H₂].
  1. x²/(0.1 − x)² = 4.24
  2. Take root: x/(0.1 − x) = 2.06
  3. x = 0.067 M
  4. [CO] = [H₂O] = 0.033 M; [CO₂] = [H₂] = 0.067 M

cards.term: Shortcut for Problem 6.4? (trick)
cards.definition: Both sides are perfect squares: take square roots instead of solving the quadratic

cards.term: Kp for 2NOCl ⇌ 2NO + Cl₂, Kc = 3.75 × 10⁻⁶ at 1069 K? (Problem 6.5)
Correction: NCERT’s Problem 6.5 prints Kp = 0.033. Recompute.
cards.definition: 3.75 × 10⁻⁶ × 88.8 = 3.33 × 10⁻⁴; 0.033 is 100× too large

cards.term: What is a heterogeneous equilibrium?
cards.definition: Species in more than one phase, e.g. H₂O(l) ⇌ H₂O(g); Ca(OH)₂(s) ⇌ Ca²⁺ + 2OH⁻

cards.term: Why are pure solids and liquids left out of K?
cards.definition: Their molar concentration is constant, independent of amount

cards.term: K for CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g)?
cards.definition: Kp = p(CO₂); at 1100 K p(CO₂) = 2 × 10⁵ Pa → Kp = 2.00

cards.term: Kc for Ni(s) + 4CO(g) ⇌ Ni(CO)₄(g)?
cards.definition: \( K_c = \frac{[Ni(CO)_4]}{[CO]^4} \) (used to purify nickel)

cards.term: Must the pure solid be present for heterogeneous equilibrium?
cards.definition: Yes, however small, though it does not appear in K

cards.term: Units of Kc and Kp for N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂?
cards.definition: Kc: mol/L; Kp: bar (H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI: unitless)

cards.term: How can K be made dimensionless?
cards.definition: Divide by standard states: 1 bar for gases, 1 M for solutes

cards.term: Partial pressures from Kp
cards.definition: CO 0.66 bar, CO₂ 0.15 bar

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Problem 6.6

CO₂ + C(s) ⇌ 2CO, Kp = 3.0; start p(CO₂) = 0.48 bar. Equilibrium pressures?

CO₂ falls by x, CO rises by 2x.
  1. (2x)²/(0.48 − x) = 3
  2. 4x² + 3x − 1.44 = 0 → x = 0.33
  3. ?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Problem 6.6

CO₂ + C(s) ⇌ 2CO, Kp = 3.0; start p(CO₂) = 0.48 bar. Equilibrium pressures?

CO₂ falls by x, CO rises by 2x.
  1. (2x)²/(0.48 − x) = 3
  2. 4x² + 3x − 1.44 = 0 → x = 0.33
  3. p(CO) = 2x = 0.66 bar; p(CO₂) = 0.15 bar

cards.term: Correction: Problem 6.6 labels both answers "pCO₂". Which is which?
cards.definition: p(CO) = 0.66 bar (= 2x) and p(CO₂) = 0.15 bar

cards.text: Features of K: independent of {{c1::initial concentrations}}; depends on {{c2::temperature}}; reverse reaction has {{c3::1/K}}; says nothing about {{c4::rate}}.

cards.term: Magnitude of K and extent
cards.definition: Kc > 10³: Products predominate; nearly complete; Kc < 10⁻³: Reactants predominate; hardly proceeds; 10⁻³ to 10³: Appreciable reactants and products

advancedHtml.frontHtml:

cards.term: Figure 6.6 in a line?
cards.definition: Negligible ← Kc 10⁻³ … 10³ → extremely large

cards.term: What is the reaction quotient Q?
cards.definition: Same expression as K but with concentrations at any time, not necessarily equilibrium

cards.term: Predicting direction from Q and K
cards.definition: Q < K forward; Q > K reverse; Q = K equilibrium

cards.term: Direction with Q and K bars (Fig 6.7)?
cards.definition: Qc < Kc → products; Qc > Kc → reactants

cards.term: H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI (Kc 57): [H₂] 0.10, [I₂] 0.20, [HI] 0.40 M. Direction?
cards.definition: Qc = 0.16/0.02 = 8.0 < 57 → forward

cards.term: 2A ⇌ B + C, Kc = 2 × 10⁻³; all at 3 × 10⁻⁴ M. Direction? (Problem 6.7)
cards.definition: Qc = 1 > Kc → reverse

cards.term: Steps to find equilibrium concentrations (ICE)?
cards.definition: Balanced equation → table of Initial, Change (x), Equilibrium → substitute in K → solve for x → check

cards.term: N₂O₄ dissociation Kp and Kc

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Problem 6.8

13.8 g N₂O₄ in 1 L at 400 K; total p at equilibrium 9.15 bar. Kp, Kc?

Initial p from pV = nRT.
  1. n = 0.15 mol → p(N₂O₄)₀ = 0.15 × 0.083 × 400 = 4.98 bar
  2. Total: 4.98 + x = 9.15 → x = 4.17
  3. p(N₂O₄) = 0.81, p(NO₂) = 8.34 bar
  4. ?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Problem 6.8

13.8 g N₂O₄ in 1 L at 400 K; total p at equilibrium 9.15 bar. Kp, Kc?

Initial p from pV = nRT.
  1. n = 0.15 mol → p(N₂O₄)₀ = 0.15 × 0.083 × 400 = 4.98 bar
  2. Total: 4.98 + x = 9.15 → x = 4.17
  3. p(N₂O₄) = 0.81, p(NO₂) = 8.34 bar
  4. Kp = 8.34²/0.81 = 85.9; Kc = 85.9/(0.083 × 400) = 2.6

cards.term: 3.0 mol PCl₅ in 1 L at 380 K, Kc = 1.80. Composition? (Problem 6.9)
cards.definition: x²/(3 − x) = 1.8 → x = 1.59: [PCl₃] = [Cl₂] = 1.59 M, [PCl₅] = 1.41 M

cards.term: Relation of ΔG with ΔG° and Q?
cards.definition: \( \Delta G = \Delta G^{\circ} + RT \ln Q \)

cards.term: At equilibrium, ΔG° = ?
cards.definition: \( -RT \ln K \) (since ΔG = 0 and Q = K)

cards.term: K from ΔG°?
cards.definition: \( K = e^{-\Delta G^{\circ}/RT} \): ΔG° < 0 → K > 1

cards.term: Kc for glucose phosphorylation, ΔG° = 13.8 kJ/mol at 298 K? (Problem 6.10)
cards.definition: ln K = −5.569 → K = 3.81 × 10⁻³

cards.term: ΔG° for sucrose hydrolysis, Kc = 2 × 10¹³ at 300 K? (Problem 6.11)
cards.definition: −7.64 × 10⁴ J mol⁻¹

cards.term: Le Chatelier’s principle?
cards.definition: A change in any factor that determines equilibrium makes the system shift so as to counteract the change

cards.term: Effect of adding H₂ to H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI?
cards.definition: Qc < Kc → shifts forward; new [H₂] is lower than just after addition but higher than originally

cards.term: Industrial use of removing a product?
cards.definition: NH₃ is liquefied and removed; CO₂ removed from the lime kiln so CaCO₃ decomposes completely

cards.term: Fe³⁺ + SCN⁻ ⇌ [Fe(SCN)]²⁺: colours?
cards.definition: Yellow + colourless ⇌ deep red

cards.term: Adding oxalic acid or HgCl₂ to the Fe(SCN)²⁺ equilibrium?
cards.definition: Removes Fe³⁺ (as [Fe(C₂O₄)₃]³⁻) or SCN⁻ (as [Hg(SCN)₄]²⁻) → shifts back, red fades

cards.term: When does pressure (volume) change shift an equilibrium?
cards.definition: Only if gaseous moles differ (Δn ≠ 0); solids/liquids ignored

cards.term: CO + 3H₂ ⇌ CH₄ + H₂O compressed to half volume: shift?
cards.definition: Forward (4 mol gas → 2 mol); Qc becomes less than Kc

cards.term: C(s) + CO₂ ⇌ 2CO: effect of higher pressure?
cards.definition: Reverse (forward increases gas moles)

cards.term: Inert gas added at constant volume?
cards.definition: No effect: partial pressures and concentrations unchanged

cards.term: Inert gas added at constant pressure? (JEE extension)
cards.definition: Volume increases → shifts towards more gaseous moles

cards.term: How does temperature affect K?
cards.definition: Exothermic: K decreases with T. Endothermic: K increases with T. (Only T changes K.)

cards.term: 2NO₂ ⇌ N₂O₄ (ΔH = −57.2 kJ): colour in ice vs hot water?
cards.definition: Cold: paler (more N₂O₄). Hot: darker brown (more NO₂).

cards.term: [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ + 4Cl⁻ ⇌ [CoCl₄]²⁻ (endothermic): colour change on cooling?
cards.definition: Blue (room T) → pink when cooled

cards.term: Correction: NCERT writes [Co(H₂O)₆]³⁺ and calls [CoCl₄]²⁻ "colourless". Accurate?
cards.definition: It is [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ (Co²⁺, pink) and [CoCl₄]²⁻ is blue (NCERT’s own text says the mixture is blue)

cards.term: Effect of a catalyst on equilibrium?
cards.definition: Speeds forward and reverse equally (same lowering of Eₐ); no change in K or composition

cards.term: Optimum Haber conditions?
cards.definition: Iron catalyst, ~500 °C, ~200 atm

cards.term: Why not run Haber at low temperature despite higher yield?
cards.definition: Rate becomes too slow

cards.term: Contact process catalyst and why needed despite Kc = 1.7 × 10²⁶?
cards.definition: Pt or V₂O₅: SO₂ → SO₃ is very slow

cards.term: Can a catalyst help a reaction with tiny K?
cards.definition: Little help: it cannot shift equilibrium

cards.term: Mnemonic for Le Chatelier? (intuition)
cards.definition: "The system is a contrarian": add something, it uses it up; heat it, it absorbs heat; squeeze it, it makes fewer gas molecules

cards.term: Faraday’s classification of substances?
cards.definition: Electrolytes (conduct in solution) and non-electrolytes

cards.term: Strong vs weak electrolyte, with ionisation %?
cards.definition: Strong: ~100% (NaCl). Weak: partial, e.g. acetic acid < 5%.

cards.term: Why does NaCl dissolve and ionise in water?
cards.definition: Water’s high dielectric constant (80) cuts ionic attraction 80-fold; ions get hydrated

cards.term: Dissociation vs ionisation (NCERT)?
cards.definition: Dissociation: separating ions already present (NaCl). Ionisation: neutral molecule splits into ions (HCl).

cards.term: Acids in gastric juice, vinegar, lemon, tamarind?
cards.definition: HCl (1.2–1.5 L/day); acetic; citric and ascorbic; tartaric

cards.term: Origin of the word "acid"?
cards.definition: Latin "acidus": sour

cards.term: Arrhenius acids and bases?
cards.definition: Acids give H⁺(aq); bases give OH⁻(aq) in water

cards.term: Limitations of the Arrhenius concept?
cards.definition: Only for aqueous solutions; can’t explain basicity of NH₃ (no OH group)

cards.term: Why does H⁺ exist as H₃O⁺?
cards.definition: A bare proton (~10⁻¹⁵ m) has an intense field and bonds to a lone pair of water; H₃O⁺ is trigonal pyramidal

cards.term: Further hydrated forms of H₃O⁺ and OH⁻?
cards.definition: H₅O₂⁺, H₇O₃⁺, H₉O₄⁺; H₃O₂⁻, H₅O₃⁻, H₇O₄⁻

cards.term: Brönsted–Lowry acids and bases?
cards.definition: Acid = proton donor; base = proton acceptor

cards.term: What is a conjugate acid–base pair?
cards.definition: Two species differing by one proton (NH₄⁺/NH₃, H₂O/OH⁻)

cards.term: Strength relation in a conjugate pair?
cards.definition: Strong acid → weak conjugate base, and vice versa

cards.term: Conjugate bases of HF, H₂SO₄, HCO₃⁻? (Problem 6.12)
cards.definition: F⁻, HSO₄⁻, CO₃²⁻

cards.term: Conjugate acids of NH₂⁻, NH₃, HCOO⁻? (Problem 6.13)
cards.definition: NH₃, NH₄⁺, HCOOH

cards.term: Amphiprotic species
cards.definition: H₂O: H₃O⁺ / OH⁻; HCO₃⁻: H₂CO₃ / CO₃²⁻; HSO₄⁻: H₂SO₄ / SO₄²⁻; NH₃: NH₄⁺ / NH₂⁻

cards.term: Lewis acids and bases (1923)?
cards.definition: Acid = electron-pair acceptor; base = electron-pair donor

cards.term: Examples of Lewis acids and bases?
cards.definition: Acids: BF₃, AlCl₃, Co³⁺, Mg²⁺, H⁺. Bases: H₂O, NH₃, OH⁻, F⁻.

cards.term: BF₃ + NH₃ → ?
cards.definition: F₃B←NH₃: BF₃ accepts N’s lone pair

cards.term: Classify OH⁻, F⁻, H⁺, BCl₃. (Problem 6.15)
cards.definition: Lewis bases: OH⁻, F⁻. Lewis acids: H⁺, BCl₃.

cards.term: Strong acids named in NCERT?
cards.definition: HClO₄, HCl, HBr, HI, HNO₃, H₂SO₄

cards.term: Strong bases named in NCERT?
cards.definition: LiOH, NaOH, KOH, CsOH, Ba(OH)₂

cards.term: In an acid–base equilibrium, which side is favoured?
cards.definition: Towards the weaker acid and weaker base

cards.term: Very strong bases (conjugates of very weak acids)?
cards.definition: NH₂⁻, O²⁻, H⁻

cards.term: How does an indicator like phenolphthalein work?
cards.definition: It is a weak acid whose HIn and In⁻ forms have different colours

cards.term: Ionic product of water at 298 K?
Molarity of pure water, and fraction dissociated?
cards.definition: 55.55 M; about 2 in 10⁹ molecules

cards.term: Is Kw constant with temperature?
cards.definition: No: it increases with T (ionisation is endothermic), so neutral pH < 7 at higher T

cards.term: Definition of pH (strict)?
cards.definition: \( pH = -\log a_{H^+} \); for dilute solutions ≈ −log[H⁺]

cards.text: At 298 K: pH + pOH = {{c1::14}}; acidic pH {{c2::< 7}}; basic pH {{c3::> 7}}.

cards.term: A tenfold change in [H⁺] changes pH by?
cards.definition: 1 unit (100-fold → 2 units)

cards.term: pH of 10⁻² M HCl and of NaOH with [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁴ M?
cards.definition: 2 and 10

cards.term: Accuracy of pH paper vs pH meter?
cards.definition: Paper ~0.5 (four-strip paper, Fig 6.11); meter ~0.001

cards.term: pH of human blood, gastric juice, lemon juice, milk of magnesia?
cards.definition: 7.4, ~1.2, ~2.2, 10

cards.term: pH of soft drink with [H⁺] = 3.8 × 10⁻³ M? (Problem 6.16)
cards.definition: 2.42

cards.term: pH of very dilute acid

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Problem 6.17

pH of 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ M HCl?

Trap: water’s own H⁺ cannot be ignored.
  1. [H⁺] = 10⁻⁸ + x; [OH⁻] = x
  2. (10⁻⁸ + x)x = 10⁻¹⁴ → x = 9.5 × 10⁻⁸
  3. ?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Problem 6.17

pH of 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ M HCl?

Trap: water’s own H⁺ cannot be ignored.
  1. [H⁺] = 10⁻⁸ + x; [OH⁻] = x
  2. (10⁻⁸ + x)x = 10⁻¹⁴ → x = 9.5 × 10⁻⁸
  3. pOH = 7.02 → pH = 6.98

cards.term: Why isn’t pH of 10⁻⁸ M HCl equal to 8? (trap)
cards.definition: An acid can’t be basic: water supplies 10⁻⁷ M H⁺, far more than the acid

cards.term: Ka for weak acid HX in terms of c and α?
cards.definition: \( K_a = \frac{c\alpha^2}{1 - \alpha} \approx c\alpha^2 \)

cards.term: Ostwald dilution law shortcut for weak acids?
cards.definition: \( \alpha \approx \sqrt{K_a / c} \), \( [H^+] \approx \sqrt{K_a c} \)

cards.term: Strongest and weakest acid in Table 6.6?
cards.definition: Strongest: HNO₂ (4.5 × 10⁻⁴); weakest: phenol (1.3 × 10⁻¹⁰)

cards.term: Define pKa. Larger pKa means?
cards.definition: pKa = −log Ka; larger pKa → weaker acid

cards.term: Degree of ionisation of HF

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Problem 6.18

0.02 M HF, Ka = 3.2 × 10⁻⁴. α, species and pH?

Ka ≫ Kw, so HF ionisation is the main reaction.
  1. 0.02α²/(1 − α) = 3.2 × 10⁻⁴
  2. ?
  3. [H₃O⁺] = [F⁻] = 2.4 × 10⁻³ M; [HF] = 17.6 × 10⁻³ M
  4. pH = 2.62
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Problem 6.18

0.02 M HF, Ka = 3.2 × 10⁻⁴. α, species and pH?

Ka ≫ Kw, so HF ionisation is the main reaction.
  1. 0.02α²/(1 − α) = 3.2 × 10⁻⁴
  2. α = 0.12
  3. [H₃O⁺] = [F⁻] = 2.4 × 10⁻³ M; [HF] = 17.6 × 10⁻³ M
  4. pH = 2.62

cards.term: 0.1 M monobasic acid has pH 4.50. Ka and pKa? (Problem 6.19)
cards.definition: [H⁺] = 3.16 × 10⁻⁵; Ka = 1.0 × 10⁻⁸, pKa = 8

cards.term: pH and % dissociation of 0.08 M HOCl, Ka = 2.5 × 10⁻⁵? (Problem 6.20)
cards.definition: [H⁺] = 1.41 × 10⁻³; 1.76%; pH 2.85

cards.term: Kb for weak base in terms of c and α?
cards.definition: \( K_b = \frac{c\alpha^2}{1 - \alpha} \)

cards.term: Weakest and strongest base in Table 6.7?
cards.definition: Strongest: dimethylamine (5.4 × 10⁻⁴); weakest: urea (1.3 × 10⁻¹⁴)

cards.term: Kb of 0.004 M hydrazine with pH 9.7? (Problem 6.21)
cards.definition: [OH⁻] = 5.98 × 10⁻⁵; Kb = 8.96 × 10⁻⁷, pKb = 6.04

cards.term: pH of 0.2 M NH₄Cl + 0.1 M NH₃, pKb = 4.75? (Problem 6.22)
cards.definition: [OH⁻] = 0.88 × 10⁻⁵ → pH 8.95

cards.term: Relation between Ka and Kb of a conjugate pair?
cards.definition: \( K_a \times K_b = K_w \); pKa + pKb = 14

cards.term: Ka of NH₄⁺ from Kb(NH₃) = 1.77 × 10⁻⁵?
cards.definition: 5.64 × 10⁻¹⁰

cards.term: α and pH of 0.05 M NH₃? (Problem 6.23)
cards.definition: α = 0.018, [OH⁻] = 9.4 × 10⁻⁴, pH = 10.97

cards.term: K for a net reaction made by adding reactions?
cards.definition: \( K_{net} = K_1 \times K_2 \times \dots \)

cards.term: What are polybasic (polyprotic) acids?
cards.definition: Acids with more than one ionisable proton: oxalic, H₂SO₄, H₃PO₄

cards.term: Why is Ka₂ < Ka₁?
cards.definition: Harder to remove H⁺ from a negatively charged ion

cards.term: Acid strength down a group (HF → HI)? Deciding factor?
cards.definition: Increases: HF ≪ HCl ≪ HBr ≪ HI; weaker H–A bond (size) decides

cards.term: Acid strength across a period (CH₄ → HF)? Deciding factor?
cards.definition: Increases: CH₄ < NH₃ < H₂O < HF; bond polarity (electronegativity) decides

cards.term: Which is the stronger acid, H₂S or H₂O?
cards.definition: H₂S (weaker, longer H–S bond)

cards.term: What is the common ion effect?
cards.definition: Suppression of ionisation by adding a substance that supplies an ion already present; a Le Chatelier effect

cards.term: pH of 0.05 M acetic acid + 0.05 M acetate, Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵?
cards.definition: [H⁺] = Ka → pH = 4.74

cards.term: Half-neutralised ammonia

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Problem 6.24

50 mL 0.10 M NH₃ + 25 mL 0.10 M HCl. pH before and after? (Kb 1.77 × 10⁻⁵)

Half the NH₃ is neutralised.
  1. Before: [OH⁻] = √(1.77×10⁻⁶) = 1.33 × 10⁻³ → pH 11.12
  2. 5 mmol NH₃ − 2.5 mmol HCl → 2.5 mmol NH₃ + 2.5 mmol NH₄⁺
  3. Equal amounts: [OH⁻] = Kb = 1.77 × 10⁻⁵
  4. ?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Problem 6.24

50 mL 0.10 M NH₃ + 25 mL 0.10 M HCl. pH before and after? (Kb 1.77 × 10⁻⁵)

Half the NH₃ is neutralised.
  1. Before: [OH⁻] = √(1.77×10⁻⁶) = 1.33 × 10⁻³ → pH 11.12
  2. 5 mmol NH₃ − 2.5 mmol HCl → 2.5 mmol NH₃ + 2.5 mmol NH₄⁺
  3. Equal amounts: [OH⁻] = Kb = 1.77 × 10⁻⁵
  4. pH = 9.24

cards.term: What is salt hydrolysis?
cards.definition: Reaction of a salt’s cation/anion with water to re-form the weak acid/base, changing pH

cards.term: pH of salt solutions
cards.definition: Strong acid + strong base (NaCl): Neutral, pH 7 (no hydrolysis); Weak acid + strong base (CH₃COONa): Basic, pH > 7; Strong acid + weak base (NH₄Cl): Acidic, pH < 7; Weak acid + weak base (CH₃COONH₄): pH = 7 + ½(pKa − pKb)

cards.term: Why is CH₃COONa solution basic?
cards.definition: CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + OH⁻

cards.term: Why is NH₄Cl solution acidic?
cards.definition: NH₄⁺ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄OH + H⁺

cards.term: Special feature of weak acid–weak base salt hydrolysis?
cards.definition: Degree of hydrolysis and pH are independent of concentration

cards.term: pH of ammonium acetate, pKa 4.76, pKb 4.75? (Problem 6.25)
cards.definition: 7 + ½(0.01) = 7.005

cards.term: Define a buffer solution.
cards.definition: Resists change in pH on dilution or adding small amounts of acid/base

cards.term: Two classic buffers and their pH?
cards.definition: Acetic acid + sodium acetate ~4.75; NH₄Cl + NH₄OH ~9.25

cards.term: Henderson–Hasselbalch equation (acidic buffer)?
cards.definition: \( pH = pK_a + \log \frac{[salt]}{[acid]} \)

cards.term: Basic buffer equation?
cards.definition: \( pOH = pK_b + \log \frac{[salt]}{[base]} \)

cards.term: When is buffer pH = pKa?
cards.definition: When [salt] = [acid] (log 1 = 0)

cards.term: How do you choose an acid to make a buffer of a given pH?
cards.definition: Pick one whose pKa is close to the target pH

cards.term: Why doesn’t dilution change buffer pH?
cards.definition: The ratio [salt]/[acid] is unchanged

cards.term: Why does blood need buffering? (intuition)
cards.definition: Enzymes work in a narrow pH window (~7.4); the H₂CO₃/HCO₃⁻ buffer mops up added H⁺ or OH⁻

cards.term: Solubility categories
cards.definition: Soluble: > 0.1 M; Slightly soluble: 0.01–0.1 M; Sparingly soluble: < 0.01 M

cards.term: Condition for a salt to dissolve?
cards.definition: Solvation enthalpy must exceed lattice enthalpy; hence ionic salts don’t dissolve in non-polar solvents

cards.term: Define solubility product.
cards.definition: \( K_{sp} = [Ba^{2+}][SO_4^{2-}] \) for BaSO₄ ⇌ Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ (saturated solution)

cards.term: Molar solubility of BaSO₄, Ksp = 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁰?
cards.definition: S = √Ksp = 1.05 × 10⁻⁵ M

cards.term: General Ksp for MₓXᵧ with solubility S?
cards.definition: \( K_{sp} = x^x y^y S^{x+y} \)

cards.term: Ksp of Zr₃(PO₄)₄ in terms of S?
Solubility of A₂X₃, Ksp = 1.1 × 10⁻²³? (Problem 6.26)
cards.definition: 108 S⁵ = 1.1 × 10⁻²³ → S = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ M

cards.term: Qsp vs Ksp: precipitation or dissolution?
cards.definition: Qsp > Ksp → precipitates; Qsp < Ksp → more dissolves

cards.term: Ksp values of common salts (Table 6.9)?
cards.definition: e.g. AgCl 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰, BaSO₄ 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁰, CaCO₃ 2.8 × 10⁻⁹

cards.term: Table 6.9 continued?
cards.definition: Lead to zinc salts

cards.term: More soluble: Ni(OH)₂ (Ksp 2 × 10⁻¹⁵) or AgCN (6 × 10⁻¹⁷)? (Problem 6.27)
cards.definition: AgCN: S = 7.8 × 10⁻⁹. Ni(OH)₂: 4S³ = 2 × 10⁻¹⁵ → S = 7.9 × 10⁻⁶. Ni(OH)₂ is more soluble.

cards.term: Correction: NCERT gives S of Ni(OH)₂ as 0.58 × 10⁻⁴ M. Recompute.
cards.definition: (2 × 10⁻¹⁵ / 4)^(1/3) = 7.9 × 10⁻⁶ M; the conclusion (Ni(OH)₂ more soluble) still holds

cards.term: Trap: compare solubility by Ksp directly?
cards.definition: Only for the same formula type: convert to S first when stoichiometry differs

cards.term: Molar solubility of Ni(OH)₂ in 0.10 M NaOH? (Problem 6.28)
cards.definition: S × (0.10)² = 2 × 10⁻¹⁵ → S = 2 × 10⁻¹³ M

cards.term: How is very pure NaCl obtained by the common ion effect?
cards.definition: Pass HCl gas through saturated brine: extra Cl⁻ precipitates NaCl

cards.term: Use of common ion effect in gravimetric analysis?
cards.definition: Near-complete precipitation: Ag⁺ as AgCl, Fe³⁺ as hydroxide, Ba²⁺ as BaSO₄

cards.term: Why are phosphates more soluble at low pH?
cards.definition: H⁺ protonates the anion, lowering its concentration, so more salt dissolves

cards.term: Le Chatelier summary
cards.definition: Add reactant: Shifts forward (K unchanged); Raise T (exothermic): Shifts back; K falls; Raise p (fewer gas moles on right): Shifts forward; Inert gas, constant V: No effect; Catalyst: No effect; faster equilibrium
